mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals strong economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 300,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% in a month and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) also increase by more than 1% in the same month, it signals a strong demand in both housing and consumer sectors, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 10% and RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increased by the specified amounts in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in real GDP (GDPC1) is positive and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same quarter, it signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY increase and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 showed a YoY increase and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the same quarter.
